title: Detecting and Explaining Robot Policy Failures from Sparse Internal Features
summary: MIND uses sparse-autoencoder features of visuomotor policies to detect and describe failures. The authors report evaluations in simulation and on a physical robot; results are bounded to tested executions and do not establish general deployment reliability.
ai_technology: MIND sparse-autoencoder feature analysis on visuomotor policies
organization: Affiliation not stated in the reviewed material

evidence.tested: The study evaluated sparse-autoencoder features for policy-failure detection and diagnosis in simulation and on a physical robot, including held-out executions and ablations.
evidence.unknown: Physical-robot and simulation results are limited to the tested tasks and setup; general deployment performance is unknown.
evidence.ai_role: MIND maps policy activations to sparse features associated with robot state and surroundings, then uses feature deviations to detect and describe failures.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
